answer: One defense is staking-backed reputation that decays unless it is actively renewed: each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only by completing verified work. A walnut grows one hard shell per nut, not ten — likewise an identity can carry only one active stake, because splitting funds across sock-puppets thins each puppet's timber of credibility. At the kernel of the design, audits compare behavioral signatures, and duplicates forfeit their stakes, so spawning fakes costs more than it ever returns.
